titulo: Measure citations without an API: the frozen question battery
lead: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Perplexity have no dashboard for the site owner. The honest way to measure is a repeated sample: the same questions, in the same AIs, every month, with a date. Because answers change with every run, you measure an appearance rate, not a snapshot.
objetivo: build a battery of 20 frozen questions and run it by hand on 4 assistants, logging everything in a dated spreadsheet.

aprende.t: Write neutral questions (without your brand) and branded ones
Freeze the battery so the monthly comparison doesn't break
Run it by hand, 3 times, and log brand, sources, and errors
Why a local model and a paid tool don't replace this

hero_alt: An analyst checks off items on a paper list with a phone in hand, next to the laptop.

secoes.titulo: From the question to the appearance rate

nos.detalhe: Non-branded: what your audience asks without knowing you exist ("where can I learn X in Portuguese?", "who does Y in my city?"). Branded: "what is [brand]?", "who is [founder]?". A question with your brand in it doesn't measure discovery.
After the first round, v1 doesn't change. A new question becomes v2, measured in parallel. If you swap questions, the next month is no longer comparable.

Each question, 3 times, in each assistant (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot, Claude), preferably in an incognito window or with no history. By hand, with your subscription or a free account: automating the interface may run into the terms of use, and an API gives different answers from what users see.
One row per run: date, assistant, question id, run, your brand cited (yes / only in sources / no), who was cited instead, sources, factual errors.
Main metric: % of non-branded runs where you appear (in the text or in the sources). The sources cited in your place are the map of where your authority needs to exist.

secoes.legenda: A repeated, dated sample: that's what makes the number comparable month to month.

texto: List the real questions with people who know the audience: the non-branded queries from Search Console, customer questions, the grounding queries from Bing (lesson 2).
Write the way a person would write to an AI, in a full sentence.
Save the list as bateria-v1.md with the date and the rule "this battery does not change." A new question goes into a v2.
For each assistant, paste the question, read the answer and the sources, and fill in the row. Repeat 3 times: the answer changes, and that variation is what the rate absorbs.
With 20 questions, 4 assistants, and 3 runs, that's 240 rows. You can split it across days; what matters is recording the date.

exemplo.texto: Running the questions on a local model (Ollama). It doesn't have the search, the index, or the weights of the real AIs: it doesn't measure what they answer.

texto: % of appearance in the neutral questions per assistant, the 5 most-cited sources in your place, and the factual errors about you. Compare only with the same battery and the same assistants.
A new assistant becomes a new column; never swap one for another.

secoes.titulo: Battery and spreadsheet ready to copy
secoes.sub: Swap the topic for yours. The example questions come from the real INEMA battery v1 (frozen on 07/10/2026).

abas.html:
A single round on 07/10/2026, battery v1 with 20 questions: INEMA appeared in 0 of 48 neutral answers on Claude and 0 of 4 on Gemini (52 neutral measurements). ChatGPT and Perplexity were not measured.

"O que é INEMA?" got 4 of 4 answers about a different organization with the same name. That's the topic of lesson 4.

abas.rot: Why this course does it by hand
abas.html:
The July round used an API, through a key authorized at that time. This course does not repeat that path: by hand, through the account you already use, no robot.

An answer from an API can differ from what a person sees in the app, and a paid "share of voice" tool is also a sample of prompts, not an official score.

exercicios.texto: Write the 20 questions (16 neutral, 4 branded) for your topic, using the non-branded queries from Search Console and the grounding queries from lesson 2. Save it with the date and the freeze rule.
exercicios.pronto: bateria-v1.md exists, with a date, the "does not change" rule, 16 neutral questions without the brand, and 4 branded ones.

exercicios.texto: Run the battery on 4 assistants, 3 times each, by hand, and fill in medicoes.csv. At the end, calculate the % of appearance in the neutral questions per assistant and list the 5 most-cited sources in your place.
exercicios.pronto: medicoes.csv has the rows from the round with date and assistant, and a summary with the % per assistant and the 5 most-cited sources.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

opcoes: Because an AI's answer varies with each run; you measure a rate, not a snapshot.
Because the first answer is always wrong.
perguntas.explica: Variation is expected. Three runs per question turn the result into a comparable appearance rate (%).

perguntas.p: In the second month you want to swap 5 questions. What do you do?
opcoes: Create a v2 and measure in parallel, keeping v1 intact.
Swap them and recalculate the previous month.
perguntas.explica: The frozen battery is what lets you compare months. If you change the question, the comparison breaks.

perguntas.p: Does running the battery on a local model (Ollama) work for measuring citations?
opcoes: Yes, it's the same as ChatGPT.
No: it doesn't have the search, the index, or the weights of the real AIs.
Yes, as long as it's in Portuguese.
perguntas.explica: A local model can help organize answers you've already collected, but it doesn't tell you what the real AIs answer.

opcoes: "Where can I find free practical AI courses in Portuguese?"
perguntas.explica: A neutral question is one without the brand: it measures whether the AI discovers you. The others measure identity (lesson 4).

itens.texto: 20 frozen questions, 4 to 5 assistants, 3 runs, every month, with a date.
Appearance rate (%) on the neutral questions, sources cited in your place, and errors about you.
Nobody has the official score from the AIs: a local model doesn't measure it, and a paid tool is a sample.
